title: Extract a Series
instructions: Return the price column as a Series.
hint: Use single square brackets around the column name.

explanation.meaning: The supplied DataFrame.
One column label inside single brackets selects a Series, not a DataFrame.

title: Preserve two dimensions
instructions: Return the price column as a one-column DataFrame (not a Series).
hint: Double brackets preserve the DataFrame structure.

explanation.meaning: The supplied DataFrame.
The inner list selects column labels; the outer brackets index the DataFrame. The result stays two-dimensional.

title: Select two columns
instructions: Return only the price and volume columns, in that order.
hint: Pass a list of column labels.

explanation.meaning: The supplied DataFrame.
A list of two column labels selects both columns in the specified order.

title: Find a labeled cell
instructions: Get the single price value for ticker MSFT (scalar).
hint: Use .loc[row_label, column_label].

explanation.meaning: Label-based lookup (not numerical positions).
The row index label to find.
The column label to find. Selecting one row and one column gives a scalar.

title: Rectangular selection
instructions: Keep rows AAPL and NVDA, and columns price and return_1d, in that order.
hint: Use .loc with a list of row labels and a list of column labels.

explanation.meaning: Select by row and column labels.
The exact row labels to keep, in this order.
The exact column labels to keep, in this order.

title: Positional slicing
instructions: Return the first three rows and first two columns using positions.
hint: Use .iloc and slice endpoints; stop positions are excluded.

explanation.meaning: Position-based selection: positions start at zero.
Rows from position 0 up to, but not including, 3.
Columns from position 0 up to, but not including, 2.

title: Single positional element
instructions: Return the scalar in the third row and second column.
hint: Both .iloc positions are zero-based.

explanation.meaning: Select by numerical positions rather than labels.
Row position 2, i.e. the third row.
Column position 1, i.e. the second column. Two integer selectors return a scalar.

title: Keep a single row 2D
instructions: Return the second row, preserving a one-row DataFrame.
hint: Wrapping the position in a list retains the row dimension.

explanation.meaning: Index using row positions.
The inner list contains one row position. A list preserves a two-dimensional DataFrame; a bare 1 would give a Series.

title: Volume threshold
instructions: Keep stocks with volume strictly above {threshold}. Return only price and return_1d columns.
hint: Construct a Boolean mask, then use .loc[mask, columns].

explanation.meaning: Compare each volume to the threshold, producing a Boolean Series.
The first .loc argument chooses rows; the second chooses columns.
Keep only these columns in this order.

title: Combined condition
instructions: Keep rows with price above {threshold} AND a positive return_1d. Return price and return_1d.
hint: Parenthesize each condition before using &.

explanation.meaning: First elementwise condition: price above the threshold.
Second elementwise condition: positive daily return.
Combine Boolean Series with elementwise AND; parentheses are required around comparisons.
Use the combined mask to filter rows and select the requested columns.

title: Membership filtering
instructions: Return sector and volume for stocks in Technology or Financials.
hint: Use .isin([...]) to test membership.

explanation.meaning: The sector column, as a Series.
True when each sector value belongs to this list.
Keep matching rows and two specified columns.

title: Build a Boolean Series
instructions: Return a Boolean Series indicating which stocks had a positive return_1d.
hint: A comparison to a scalar returns a Boolean Series.

explanation.meaning: Return the daily-return Series.
Compare each element with zero; the output is a Boolean Series retaining its index.

title: Filter a range
instructions: Return only the pe column for stocks with pe between {lo} and {hi}, inclusive. Keep the result as a DataFrame.
hint: Combine .between(lo, hi) and a one-element column list.

explanation.meaning: Extract the price-to-earnings column.
True when the value falls between the bounds, inclusive by default.
Filter matching rows and retain the output as a one-column DataFrame.

title: Sort and select
instructions: Sort rows by return_1d descending and return only price and return_1d.
hint: Use sort_values(..., ascending=False).

explanation.meaning: Sort rows by daily return, highest first.
After sorting, keep exactly these two columns.

title: Top volume stocks
instructions: Return the three stocks with highest volume, showing volume and price in that order.
hint: Try .nlargest(3, "volume").

explanation.meaning: Keep the three rows with the highest trading volume, ordered descending.
Select and reorder the resulting columns.

title: Invert a mask
instructions: Return only price for stocks NOT in Technology; preserve a DataFrame.
hint: Negate a Boolean mask with ~; parenthesize compound masks.

explanation.meaning: Create a Boolean Series for Technology rows.
Invert each Boolean value; True becomes False and vice versa.
Keep non-Technology rows and only their price column, as a DataFrame.

title: Computed column
instructions: Add a column notional equal to price × volume. Return the entire DataFrame with the new column at the end.
hint: assign creates a new DataFrame with the extra column.

explanation.meaning: Multiply the two Series elementwise, matching their indices.
Name the new column notional.
Return a new DataFrame with the additional column; the original input remains unchanged.

title: Absolute returns
instructions: Return a Series of the absolute values of return_1d.
hint: Series.abs() gives elementwise absolute values.

explanation.meaning: Select the Series of daily returns.
Return absolute values elementwise; negative returns become positive magnitudes.

title: Price scaling
instructions: Return the price Series multiplied by {factor} and rounded to two decimals.
hint: Multiply the Series before calling .round(2).

explanation.meaning: The price Series.
Multiply every price by the supplied factor (vectorized arithmetic).
Round each resulting value to two decimal places.

title: Integer volume buckets
instructions: Return a Series whose elements are volume floor-divided by {divisor}.
hint: The // operator performs elementwise floor division.

explanation.meaning: Select volume as a Series.
Floor-divide each element by the divisor, discarding any remainder.

title: Ranks
instructions: Return a Series ranking return_1d in descending order, using the min method for ties.
hint: Series.rank has ascending and method parameters.

explanation.meaning: The return Series to rank.
Rank values instead of sorting rows.
Rank largest returns first (rank 1 is highest).
Tied values receive the lowest rank occupied by that tie group.

title: Center a Series
instructions: Subtract the mean price from every price and return the resulting Series.
hint: A scalar subtracts from every value in a Series.

explanation.meaning: Compute one scalar: the mean of the price column.
Subtract the same scalar from every element, yielding a mean-centered Series.

title: Sum by trade side
instructions: Return a Series containing summed qty by side (BUY and SELL).
hint: Group on side, select qty, aggregate with .sum().

explanation.meaning: Partition trade rows by BUY versus SELL.
Choose the quantity column from each group.
Sum quantities separately within each group, returning a Series indexed by side.

title: Aggregate by symbol
instructions: Return summed quantities by symbol as a Series, sorted by symbol.
hint: Use groupby on symbol followed by qty.sum().

explanation.meaning: Form a group for each distinct ticker symbol.
Choose quantities within each ticker group.
Compute total traded quantity per ticker.

title: Trade counts
instructions: Return a Series counting rows for each symbol.
hint: groupby(...).size() counts rows, including those with missing values.

explanation.meaning: Group trades by ticker.
Count rows in each group, including rows with missing values in other columns.

title: Mean execution price
instructions: Return a Series of mean trade price by symbol.
hint: Select price before .mean().

explanation.meaning: Group rows by ticker.
Choose trade prices.
Compute the arithmetic mean trade price in each ticker group.

title: Two-level grouping
instructions: Return counts of trades grouped by symbol and then side as a MultiIndex Series.
hint: Pass a list of grouping columns.

explanation.meaning: Group by combinations of two keys, producing a MultiIndex.
Count trades for every symbol/side combination.

title: Aggregate computed notional
instructions: For each symbol, sum qty × price. Return the totals as a Series named notional.
hint: Create notional with assign, then group and sum.

explanation.meaning: Compute notional traded value per row.
Add that derived column to a new DataFrame.
Collect notional values by ticker.
Sum notional within each ticker group.

title: Multi-aggregation
instructions: Return a DataFrame by symbol, with total_qty (sum of qty) and avg_price (mean price), in that order.
hint: Named aggregation uses new_name=(column, function).

explanation.meaning: Group trade rows by ticker.
Apply multiple named aggregations, producing a DataFrame.
Create total_qty from the sum of qty.
Create avg_price from the mean of price.

title: Average return per asset
instructions: Return a Series of average returns, one entry per asset.
hint: Aggregate down the rows (axis=0).

explanation.meaning: The full time-by-asset return DataFrame.
Aggregate down rows (time), producing one mean return per column (asset).

title: Select assets
instructions: Return only AAPL and NVDA columns, as a DataFrame.
hint: Use a list of column labels.

explanation.meaning: The returns DataFrame.
Keep only the AAPL and NVDA columns; double brackets keep two dimensions.

title: Daily return spread
instructions: Return the daily AAPL minus MSFT return spread as a Series.
hint: Subtract two aligned Series.

explanation.meaning: The AAPL return Series.
The MSFT return Series.
Subtract elementwise, aligned by date index; the result is a Series.

title: Correlation matrix
instructions: Return the full Pearson correlation matrix between asset return columns.
hint: DataFrame.corr() computes pairwise column correlations.

explanation.meaning: The matrix of asset returns over dates.
Compute the pairwise Pearson correlation across columns, returning a square asset-by-asset matrix.

title: Moving average
instructions: Return the 3-day rolling mean DataFrame, using the default min_periods.
hint: Chain .rolling(3) and .mean().

explanation.meaning: Create a moving window of three consecutive rows per column.
Average each window. The first two rows are NaN because a full window is not yet available.

title: Cumulative returns
instructions: Return the cumulative compounded simple returns for each asset, computed as (1 + r).cumprod() - 1.
hint: Apply cumprod column-wise after adding one.

explanation.meaning: Convert each simple return into a gross return factor.
Multiply factors cumulatively down the date axis.
Convert the cumulative gross factors back into cumulative simple returns.

title: Cross-sectional mean
instructions: For each date, return the average across all four assets as a Series.
hint: axis=1 aggregates across the columns.

explanation.meaning: Dates are rows and assets are columns.
Aggregate across columns within each row; gives one mean across assets for each date.

title: Slice first rows
instructions: Return the first two rows of arr, keeping all columns.
hint: First index slices rows, second slices columns.

explanation.meaning: The supplied NumPy matrix.
Before the comma selects rows 0–1 (stop 2 excluded); after the comma selects all columns.

title: Extract a column
instructions: Return the third column of arr as a one-dimensional NumPy array.
hint: Use : for all rows and integer 2 for column index.

explanation.meaning: The supplied NumPy matrix.
Keep every row and select column position 2. Integer indexing removes the column dimension, yielding a 1D array.

title: Keep a dimension
instructions: Return the third column of arr as a two-dimensional array with shape (5, 1).
hint: Slice 2:3 rather than indexing with integer 2.

explanation.meaning: The supplied NumPy matrix.
Keep all rows and slice columns from 2 through before 3. A slice retains a 2D column dimension.

title: Boolean matrix
instructions: Return a Boolean array marking elements strictly above {threshold}.
hint: Vectorized comparison produces a Boolean array.

explanation.meaning: The NumPy array.
Compare every element to the threshold using broadcasting, returning a Boolean array of the same shape.

title: Filter rows using column
instructions: Keep only rows where the first column is strictly greater than {threshold}; retain all columns.
hint: First construct a row mask with arr[:,0].

explanation.meaning: Take column 0 for every row, producing a 1D array.
Create one Boolean selector per row.
Use that mask to keep whole rows from the original matrix.

title: Column sums
instructions: Return column sums of arr as a 1D array.
hint: axis=0 collapses the row axis.

explanation.meaning: Sum values along a specified axis.
Collapse the row axis; obtain one sum per column.

title: Row sums
instructions: Return row sums of arr as a 1D array.
hint: axis=1 collapses the column axis.

explanation.meaning: Sum values along a specified axis.
Collapse the column axis; obtain one sum per row.

title: Transpose axes
instructions: Transpose the matrix: return arr with its axes swapped.
hint: A 2D array transposes with .T.

explanation.meaning: The source NumPy matrix, here 5 rows by 6 columns.
Transpose: swap axis 0 and axis 1, turning an (m, n) array into (n, m). No sorting occurs.

title: Column slice
instructions: Keep all rows but only columns at positions 1, 2, and 3.
hint: Slicing excludes the stop index.

explanation.meaning: The original NumPy matrix.
Select all rows and column positions 1, 2, and 3; the stop index 4 is exclusive.

title: Reshape elements
instructions: Reshape arr from 5×6 to 3×10 without changing element order.
hint: reshape retains element order by default.

explanation.meaning: The original NumPy array.
Reinterpret the 30 elements as 3 rows by 10 columns, using NumPy’s default C-order traversal.

title: Broadcast column means
instructions: Subtract each column mean from the corresponding column in arr, producing a float matrix.
hint: A shape-(6,) vector broadcasts over 5 rows.

explanation.meaning: Compute the column means as a 1D array.
Subtract these column means from every row via broadcasting; the result retains the matrix shape.

title: Conditional values
instructions: Return an integer array containing 1 for even elements and 0 for odd elements.
hint: np.where(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false).

explanation.meaning: Remainder 0 after division by 2 identifies even elements, returning a Boolean array.
Return 1 where the condition is true and 0 otherwise, preserving the input shape.

title: Filter a vector
instructions: Return only values strictly greater than {threshold}.
hint: Use a Boolean mask as an index.

explanation.meaning: Create a Boolean mask by comparing each vector element.
Use the mask to keep only values above the threshold.

title: Vector to matrix
instructions: Reshape the 12-element vector arr into a 3×4 matrix.
hint: 3 × 4 = 12 elements.

explanation.meaning: A 1D NumPy array containing 12 elements.
Create a 3-by-4 matrix. The element count stays 12.

title: Cumulative vector sum
instructions: Return the cumulative sum of arr.
hint: Use np.cumsum or arr.cumsum().

explanation.meaning: The source 1D array.
Return cumulative sums: each output element includes all values up through that position.
